outcome: mode of delivery (operative vaginal delivery, LSCS rates)
duration of first stage of labour
duration of second stage of labour
cohort: Nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies in labour, divided into groups with and without Lumbar Epidural Analgesia.
finding: Lumbar Epidural Analgesia increased operative vaginal delivery rates but decreased LSCS rates, shortened the duration of the first stage of labour, and had no significant effect on the second stage of labour or neonatal APGAR scores.
mod_finding: Epidural analgesia was associated with increased operative vaginal delivery rates but significantly decreased LSCS rates in nulliparous women.
cross-section timing: During labour and immediately post-birth for neonatal assessment.
